messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: hosted-runtime gpupool-7 experiencing repeated OOMs tied to KV cache growth. Affected services: text-gen (v2), streaming. Error rate spike to 12% over last 5m. Auto-evict failing.

matt_oncall: on-call here, grabbing pager. seeing memory climb in metrics, large number of long-session requests (>> 65k tokens).

priya: linking dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/kvcache/gpupool-7?view=oom — looks like continuous batching config changed 03:10 UTC (batch_window_ms 120 -> 250) rolled 6 hours ago.

sasha: confirmed config change. recent rollout added more aggressive prefix prefetch + higher batch window. suspect increased KV retention and larger windows causing kvcache map to blow up for long prompts.

carla_reliability: customers X/Y reported transient 500s. CS alerted a handful of enterprise early adopters. No total outage but elevated latency and tail errors.

jason_runtime: grabbing logs from pod text-gen-5:
```
I2026-03-17T03:35:12.456Z runtime: kvcache: new_entry token_count=987654 session_id=abcd... mem_delta=+3.1GB
E2026-03-17T03:35:13.019Z runtime: OOM: alloc failed at kvcache::insert
```
Looks like single sessions with runaway tokens causing huge inserts; eviction policy not kicking in due to batch window holding references.

matt_oncall: mitigation options: 1) instant rollback of batch_window to 120ms, 2) apply session-length caps (max_kv_tokens=20000) as hotfix, 3) emergency prefetch throttle to disable prefetch for hosted tier. What's fastest?

priya: fastest is toggling prefetch throttle to ON for gpupool-7 (no deploy). second-fastest is cluster config rollback (requires rollout, ~3m). session cap needs code flag flip but we can gate via dynamic config.

sasha: I'll flip prefetch throttle now (cmd):
```
curl -X POST "https://controlplane/api/pools/gpupool-7/config" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prefetch_enabled":false}'
```
Applying and watching.

incident-bot: Action recorded: prefetch throttle applied to gpupool-7 by sasha at 6605001251.

matt_oncall: seeing immediate drop in new kvcache allocations. mem pressure stabilizing. eviction resumed.

carla_reliability: notifying CS: "We applied an emergency throttle for prefetch on a subset of hosted runtime to restore stability. No data loss. We're monitoring and will follow up in 30m."

support-ops: forwarded affected customer list to eng + CS. ticket IDs: #18923, #18924.

jason_runtime: starting a targeted canary rollback of batch_window to 120ms for gpupool-7 (patch) — will keep prefetch throttle disabled until canary stable.

priya: also adding a dynamic session-length guard rule into runtime config: max_kv_tokens=20000 for hosted tier; if session exceeds, runtime truncates KV prefetch and streams warning in logs. This should be staged after stability.

matt_oncall: current plan timeline: 1) emergency throttle applied (done) 2) observe 10m — if stable, push batch_window rollback canary (jason) 3) if stable at 30m, roll to rest of pool and remove throttle 4) schedule followup postmortem + customer comms.

sasha: metrics 2m after throttle: OOMs -> 0, eviction rate back to baseline, p95 latency improved. Good sign.

carla_reliability: customer impact log entry added. severity: P2 (service degradation). CS will send an initial outbound by EOD.

jason_runtime: canary rollback complete on 3/3 pods in pool. No regressions in 4m. proceeding to roll remaining pods.

incident-bot: Pager resolved for gpupool-7 at 6605001296. Summary: prefetch throttle + batch_window rollback mitigated runaway kvcache growth; followups required.

matt_oncall: handing off to priya for morning monitoring and root-cause followup. Priya — you'll get the runbook + links.

priya: got it, will take handoff. I'll schedule short RCA sync and recommend: revert aggressive batching change, add dynamic session caps and telemetry to detect runaway sessions earlier, add eviction backpressure when kvcache insert rate spikes.

carla_reliability: assign postmortem owners: jason (runtime), sasha (prefetch), matt (oncall notes), carla (customer comms).

support-ops: we've opened follow-up tickets to contact impacted customers and include mitigation timeline.

matt_oncall: closing pager note. Thanks team. :slightly_smiling_face:
